newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Newcrest shares jump on Quinn resignation.
newsitem.headline: Newcrest shares jump on Quinn resignation.

text.p: The share price of gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd jumped by more than eight percent on Wednesday morning following the company's surprise announcement that managing director John Quinn had resigned.

Newcrest shares reached a morning peak of A$3.50 each in quick response to the announcement, a rise of 29 cents on Tuesday's closing price. At 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), the share price had settled back to A$3.40 for a gain of 19 cents.
"Obviously it (the rise) is the Quinn resignation, or forced resignation, call it what you will," said the head of an institutional dealing desk at a European-owned brokerage firm.
Newcrest said Quinn had resigned due to differences with the board, but gave no further details.
Quinn has been temporarily replaced by former CRA Ltd group executive Ian Johnson.
It said the search for a full-time replacement had begun.
The institutional broker said the departure of Quinn would not end the problems faced by Newcrest, which has its key operation at the giant Telfer mine in Western Australia.
The mine's output was sharply curtailed earlier this year by wet weather and has faced lower grades for some time.

Newcrest has seen its share price decline sharply in recent months. From a high of A$5.40 on February 5, Newcrest shares have fallen steadily, closing Tuesday trading at A$3.21, the lowest since September 1993.
Under Quinn's direction, Newcrest attempted to be included in a complex merger of the rival gold miner Normany Mining Ltd's group in February 1996.
The bid failed, leaving Newcrest with an unwanted 11.9 percent stake in Normandy.
"I don't think it (Quinn's departure) solves all their problems," the institutional dealer said.
"I think their problem is with a balance sheet that is having a hole burnt in it," the dealer said, also citing the problems at the 350,000 ounce-a year-plus Telfer mine and low gold prices.
